title: Deadlocks

answers: Wrap both in one Mutex, or always take them in one fixed order
Add a sleep between the locks
writing.exampleCaption: Two orders, one hang. The types all check out.
writing.explanation: The borrow checker knows nothing about the order in which you take locks, so two threads taking Mutex A then Mutex B, and B then A, will still hang. The standard answers are a global lock order, holding one lock at a time, using try_lock with a timeout, or removing shared state entirely by moving to channels. Knowing Rust does not solve this is the point of the question.
writing.feedback: One lock, or one documented order, removes the cycle entirely.
